_note: Ground truth for roof STRUCTURE, drawn by Josh on renders from src/mark_roofs.py. Every automated signal tried (plane fit, fold fraction, fold depth, fold location, acceptance threshold) failed to separate roofs he calls correct from ones he calls wrong, so this is the only reference that works. Score against it; do not tune against a metric alone.

roofs.structure: TRACED FROM JOSH'S MARKUP (see traced_lines_nztm). Two hipped sections end to end, separated by a FULL-WIDTH middle section that runs eave to eave, about 5.5 x 5.2 m, split by one diagonal into two faces. The 8 faces are: NW hip triangle, SE hip triangle, the NE and SW slopes of the NW section, the NE and SW slopes of the SE section, and the two halves of the middle section.
roofs.marked: red = ridges/hips, green = true roof outline, yellow = the plane surfaces
roofs.key_finding: The face COUNT is not the test and matching it hid a wrong roof for a long time. The middle feature is not a patch inside one slope, it spans the full width of the roof from eave to eave, so it divides BOTH main slopes. The two halves of each slope are therefore separate faces in Josh's drawing, and a same-plane merge that rejoins them is wrong on this roof however coplanar they measure.

traced_lines_nztm._note: Traced from Josh's marked image against the metre grid mark_roofs.py draws (x 1258400/405/410/415, y 5004850/855/860/865). Read off by eye, so coordinates are good to roughly +/-0.3 m; the TOPOLOGY is exact and is what should be scored against. An earlier version of this file claimed the green roof outline was the footprint shifted 1.3 m NE. That was wrong -- an artefact of tracing by eye. Measured over 23 pilot buildings, the best-fit translation of footprint onto roof has a median of 0.50 m in scattered directions and lifts roof-point coverage only 77.8% -> 79.6%, so there is no systematic offset. What this roof actually has is overhang on several sides at once, which no translation fixes.

roofs.middle_section_is: RECESSED (confirmed by Josh). Measured: the ridge sits at 381.42 m, falls to 380.26 m across the middle, and returns to 381.47 m -- a 1.16 m drop. It is therefore findable as a 2-D REGION of points below the roof's own plane envelope, not as shoulders in a 1-D ridge profile, which is what earlier attempts looked for and why their band edges landed in the wrong place.

roofs.structure: Three planes. One large plane on the right taking most of the roof, one large plane top-left, one small plane bottom-left. Josh: 'The largest plane on this roof has a significant angle/slope on it. I haven't marked that. It's also still all one plane though.'
roofs.marked: red = ridges/level changes, green = true roof outline, yellow = the plane surfaces
roofs.key_finding: A plane can carry significant slope and still be ONE plane. Imagery line detection sees a line across that sloped face -- a seam, stain or tonal band -- which is not a roof line. This is what motivated _line_is_real: cut a strong imagery line only where the plane ORIENTATION changes across it, or the two sides sit at different heights. The green roof outline again runs past the LINZ footprint, here mostly on the eastern side.

roofs.structure: Two roof sections side by side, each split by a ridge into an upper and a lower plane -- four large planes -- plus one small plane on the lower-left extension. Josh: '5 in total, with 4 large ones and 1 small one'.
roofs.marked: red = ridges, green = true roof outline, blue = obstructions, yellow = the plane surfaces
roofs.key_finding: First obstruction ground truth. Josh marked ~10, mostly 1-2 m skylights; the pipeline found 4 covering 8.5 m2. Skylights sit near flush so the height path cannot see them, and the colour path scores LOCAL contrast which a bright panel on a variably-lit roof does not always clear. The top decile of roof brightness gives 9 compact blobs -- see detect_bright_objects.

roofs.structure: Josh: 'a very complicated roof'. Two multi-gabled sections, terracotta on one side and grey on the other, with many ridges, hips, valleys and dormers. He marked the lines but not the plane surfaces. This is the exception to his 1-10 planes guidance.
roofs.marked: red = ridges/hips/valleys, green = true roof outline, blue = obstructions (small dots)
roofs.key_finding: Caught brightness-based skylight detection inventing objects. Its threshold was taken PER FACET, and a percentile always finds something -- a tenth of any facet is in its own top decile -- so on this uniformly sunlit terracotta roof it manufactured 8 blobs totalling 21 m2, carving 17% of a 149 m2 roof down to 9 panels against Josh's 7 small dots. Taking the threshold over the whole roof instead: 0 false blobs here, 8 real skylights still found on 29 Edinburgh.

roofs.obstruction_share_marked: roughly a quarter to a third of the roof
roofs.structure: Large commercial roof, 1054 m2 footprint, heavily covered in plant: ducting, walkways, condensers, a large central plant block. Some level changes marked in red.
roofs.marked: red = level changes/ridges, green = true roof outline, blue = obstructions (merged where close together)
roofs.key_finding: Under-detection on plant-covered commercial roofs, and neither obvious lever fixes it. The pipeline carves 16% where Josh marks roughly 25-30%. Lowering HEIGHT_RESIDUAL_THRESHOLD_M makes it WORSE (16% -> 11%), because more flagged points grow clusters that then trip the over-carve caps and are discarded whole -- a mechanism already documented in obstruction_detection.py. Relaxing those caps from 0.35/0.50 to 0.90/0.95 moves it only 16% -> 17%, so the caps are not binding either. The height path simply does not flag the plant: 2021 LiDAR at ~0.42 m spacing against ducting that is obvious in 0.1 m 2026 imagery. This is the case for an imagery-based obstruction detector.

roofs.structure: Josh: "No ridges on robins road, one clear flat face, then a secondary patio roof quite small at the top right. I have marked it as an obstruction as panels wouldn't go there. But the rest of the roof is one flat plane." One plane, 81 m2 footprint.
roofs.marked: green = true roof outline, blue = obstructions (the patio roof and one small object)

traced_obstructions_nztm._note: Traced against the metre grid (x 1258155/160, y 5004940/945/950); good to about +/-0.3 m.

roofs.key_finding: Josh later ruled that patio and carport roofs should be INCLUDED as roof by default, so modelling this patio as roof was RIGHT and the earlier note here calling it a miss was wrong. What stands: the pipeline found neither object he marked and invented a 1.2 m2 blob 7.5 m from either. Geometry exact -- one face at 90.9% on-plane, matching his one flat plane.

roofs.structure: Three red lines. The two long ones run SW-NE and divide the roof into an upper band, a darker middle band and a lower band -- the pipeline reproduces those three exactly. The third line is short (2.9 m) in the upper-left, beside the notch in the outline.
roofs.marked: green = true roof outline, red = ridges/level changes. No obstructions marked.
roofs.key_finding:
FOUR faces. Josh, on the short 2.9 m line: "The short line you mentioned upper right earlier is a small pitch change in roof that creates the different face." So it is real structure and the pipeline returns three.
Why it is invisible to the current test: splitting along that line gives slopes of 23.7 and 27.7 degrees at aspects 337.2 and 338.5 -- a 4 degree pitch change -- and BOTH halves fit 100%, as does the undivided face. Over the 2.9 m the line runs, 4 degrees is about 0.20 m of divergence, barely past the 0.15 m inlier band and only at the far edge, and the small side carries just 15 points, so the inlier fraction never falls near the 85% acceptance bar. Fit cannot see this. A PITCH difference between sub-regions can, and is the same class of signal as the fold test: structure that the residuals do not reveal.
The other two lines are reproduced exactly.
Obstructions: he marked none and the pipeline carves 1.4 m2.

roofs.structure: Josh: "Clear 4 faces on Brisbane Street". Two crossing lines divide the roof into four quadrants meeting at a point near (1258443.2, 5003984.4). Low pitch, about 10 degrees.
roofs.marked: green = true roof outline, red = ridges/valleys, blue = one small obstruction
roofs.key_finding:
GEOMETRY EXACT: four faces, arranged around a centre at (443.0, 985.1) against his crossing point at (443.2, 984.4) -- within half a metre. Aspects 229.7/49.5/228.8/52.1, fits 95.1/98.7/88.6/98.5%.
OBSTRUCTIONS 13x OVER: he marked one object of about 0.6 m2; the pipeline carves 8.0 m2 in two blobs, NEITHER overlapping his at all (1.7 m and 5.3 m away). So it misses the real object and invents two others.

roofs.structure: Josh: "5 faces on panorama terrace", labelled Face 1-5. Four parallel bands running NE-SW plus a fifth section on the right. A stepped house -- the same style he described at 7 Panorama Terrace as "lots of stepped apartment balconies".
roofs.marked: green = roof outline, red = level changes between the steps, blue = obstructions including a large structure at the bottom
roofs.key_finding:
TWO SEPARATE FAILURES, both systemic.
(1) 23.4 m2 of modelled roof sits ON the 29.9 m2 structure Josh marked as an obstruction -- we propose panels on 78% of something that cannot take them.
(2) 36.8 m2, 31% of the modelled roof, is on faces of 42.3 and 44.5 degrees. On a stepped house those are the risers between levels -- walls, not roof planes. config.MAX_ROOF_SLOPE_DEG is 72, which lets a wall through as a facet. District-wide that is 10.3% of all panels (75,430) on faces steeper than 35 degrees, carrying 27.2 GWh/yr of the claimed 294.2 -- 9.2% of the headline number.

roofs.structure: Josh: "8 faces on this one". Multi-gabled, with three obstructions marked.
roofs.key_finding: 7 faces against his 8, fits 86-94%. Closest of the complex roofs. Obstructions: 8 found covering 12.7 m2 against his 3.

roofs.structure: Josh: "8 faces here". Several parallel ridges plus a V at the lower left.
roofs.key_finding: 10 faces against his 8 -- OVER-segmented, the first roof in this batch that is. Four of the ten are under 10 m2 and three sit at 30-37.5 degrees, so the same steep-face question as Panorama Terrace applies here.

roofs.address: no address on file; behind 10 Robins Road
roofs.structure: Josh: "11 faces here". Two hipped sections end to end, each with a ridge and a hip at both ends, a flat band between them, and two small rectangular features drawn in RED -- so they are roof faces, not obstructions. About ten small obstructions marked in blue along the eastern edge.
roofs.key_finding: CLOSEST COMPLEX ROOF SO FAR: 12 faces against his 11, on 401 m2. Fits 77.8 to 98.9%, only one face below 89%. The aspects fall into four clusters of three -- about 201, 20, 111 and 293 degrees -- which is the two-hipped-section structure he drew. Obstructions: 6 found covering 16.2 m2 against his ~10, and several of ours do land in the eastern strip where his are, so this is the first roof where the obstruction layer is roughly in the right place rather than uncorrelated.

roofs.structure: Josh: "7 faces here". Hip roof with a long ridge feature marked blue down the middle.
roofs.key_finding: 10 faces against his 7, over-segmented. One face is indefensible on any reading: 10.2 m2 at 42.8 degrees fitting its own points at 29.6%. That is a wall. Also the largest overhang measured so far -- 26.3% of the roof outside the footprint, median 1.35 m out.

roofs.structure: Large commercial. Josh marked obstructions only, not ridges or outline.
roofs.key_finding: WORST RESULT IN THE SET. 4,032 m2 modelled as THREE faces, two of them 2,429 m2 and 1,158 m2 fitting their own points at 15.3% and 16.3%. A face that fits at 15% is not a plane at all -- the roof is multi-level and is being covered by two near-flat sheets laid straight across it. It ships 1,138 panels at 50% roof confidence, just above the 45% gate. This is exactly the case Josh describes: stop trying to cover everything, find the few large clean flat areas.

_metric_note: Score obstructions by AREA, not object count. Josh combines nearby obstructions when marking, so his object count is not comparable: 'I am combining obstructions together when they are close, so the counting of them might not be the best approach.'
_open_problem: 7 Anderson Heights matches Josh's face COUNT of 8 but not his structure: the central hipped feature he marked is paved over by one face. Diagnosed precisely -- that face is 75 m2 with 11% of its points more than 0.5 m off plane, _best_cut does find a cut, and the setback rule blocks it (cost 2.8 m2 against 2.0 allowed) because one line through a pyramid gains only 1.5%. A hip needs SEVERAL cuts forming a closed shape, and each is individually too small to pay for itself. Loosening the setback rule does not fix it: swept against all four drawn roofs, 2.0 gives 4/4 exact and every higher value gives 3/4 or worse, because the extra cuts are not the hip. This needs compact-feature detection, not line cutting.
_obstruction_summary: Across the three simple roofs Josh marked on 29 Aug -- 47 Robins Road, 23 Brisbane Street, 9 Brisbane Street -- he marked 13.1 m2 of obstruction in total and the pipeline detected NONE OF IT: zero overlap on every one. It carved 10.9 m2 elsewhere. Face counts on the same three roofs were exact (1, 3, 4). The obstruction layer is not mis-tuned on these roofs, it is uncorrelated with them, and that is a different kind of problem: it needs rebuilding against imagery rather than another threshold sweep.
_face_count_tally: Against Josh's markups as of 29 Aug: exact on 47 Robins (1), 9 Brisbane (4), 5 Isle (3), 29 Edinburgh (5). Under by one on 23 Brisbane (3 vs 4) and 6B Limerick (7 vs 8). Over by one on 7 Anderson (9 vs 8) and 26 Panorama (6 vs 5). Over by two on 15B Frankton (10 vs 8). Four exact of nine, and the misses are within two either way -- but the count is not the test: 7 Anderson matched his count for days while three of its faces ran across the section he drew.
_commercial_strategy: Josh, on 5372567 (3,870 m2): "For large roofs like this, with many different faces, angles, roof ridges, that are clearly commercial rooftops, it might be best to try find clear areas of flat space that are very large, to place panels on. Rather than trying to squeeze in every possible face." So on large complex roofs the objective changes: find the few big clean areas, do not chase every facet. He marked obstructions only on this one, not ridges or outline.

_josh_decisions_29aug.steep_faces: Option (a): drop a face only when it is BOTH steep AND badly fitted. Slope alone must not disqualify.
_josh_decisions_29aug.overhang: Option (a): leave roof outside the LINZ footprint out. Do not model the eave.
_josh_decisions_29aug.commercial_min_area: Ignore any clean area that would take fewer than 8 panels -- on big roofs only.
_josh_decisions_29aug.patio_carport: INCLUDE by default. Josh: "normally include these by default. This was just an example where it was transparent on top... realistically it could have panels on it if there is enough space." So 47 Robins Road's patio is NOT a miss -- modelling it as roof was right.
_josh_decisions_29aug.obstruction_metric: Do NOT score by counting obstructions. Josh: "Counting obstructions is an inaccurate metric." Score by marked AREA vs detected area, or area within a plane.
_josh_decisions_29aug.panel_orientation: Undecided: needs real layout examples at several settings for Josh to judge.
